ai_prompt_text:
Task: Convert the timetable screenshot (or file content) I send next into the sleepy-v1 plain-text format. Output nothing besides the conversion result itself - no explanations, no greetings, no markdown code fences. The first line of your output must be #sleepy-v1.

========== 1. Format rules ==========

The first line is always: #sleepy-v1

Every other line is one record, with columns separated by a vertical bar |. Three kinds of lines:

1. T line (table info, optional, at most one):
TtableName|termStartDate|totalWeeks|nodesPerDay
· The start date format is YYYY-MM-DD and must be the Monday of week 1
· Fill in only what the timetable explicitly states; leave unspecified fields empty. You may stop after the last known column, e.g. T|2026-03-02
· If the timetable does not mention these at all, omit the T line entirely. Never guess.

2. N line (per-period times, optional, one line per period):
Nnumber|startTime|endTime
· e.g. N3|10:00|10:45
· Only output N lines if the timetable explicitly provides a period-time table. Use 24-hour HH:mm; write 8:00 as 08:00
· No period-time table in the timetable -> output no N lines at all

3. C line (courses, the main body, one line per occurrence):
Cname|day|nodes|weeks|teacher|room|color|note|time|group
Always exactly 10 columns / 9 bars. Empty columns stay empty, but the bars must not be dropped. Column rules:
  Col 1 name: copy the timetable verbatim, character for character, any language
  Col 2 day: Monday..Sunday = 1 2 3 4 5 6 7
  Col 3 nodes: periods 3-4 = 3-4; single period 6 = 6
  Col 4 weeks: see "2. Week rules"
  Col 5 teacher: copy from the timetable; empty if absent
  Col 6 room: same
  Col 7 color: always empty
  Col 8 note: only if the timetable states a note; otherwise empty
  Col 9 time: only when the timetable explicitly marks a clock time for this course (e.g. evening class), as HH:mm-HH:mm; otherwise empty
  Col 10 group: always empty

========== 2. Week rules ==========

Extract the set of weeks each course meets, then decide in order:
1. A continuous range with no odd/even restriction -> S-E, e.g. 1-16
2. All odd weeks within the range ("odd weeks") -> S-E单, e.g. 1-15单
3. All even weeks ("even weeks") -> S-E双, e.g. 2-16双
4. Scattered weeks (e.g. "weeks 1-8, 10, 12-16") -> split into maximal runs, one C line each, copying all other columns:
   · A full-week run -> S-E (e.g. 1-8, 12-16)
   · A lone single week -> S定 (e.g. 10定)
   · A purely odd run -> S-E单; a purely even run -> S-E双
   · A run that is neither continuous nor purely odd/even -> S-E定 (e.g. weeks 6,7 -> 6-7定)
5. The timetable says nothing about weeks -> 1-16

========== 3. Extraction rules ==========

· A course meeting multiple times per week (different days or periods) -> multiple C lines, one per meeting; never merge into one line
· Read period numbers from "period X" in the timetable; if it has only times and no periods, number the non-overlapping time slots 1, 2, 3... top to bottom and emit matching N lines
· Copy names, teachers and rooms verbatim; if a text contains | \ " < { ( escape each with a leading \; a newline inside text is the two characters 
 and a tab is 	
· Anything the timetable does not state stays empty. Never invent teachers, rooms, times or weeks.

========== 4. Output self-check (verify silently, do not print) ==========

· First line is #sleepy-v1 and nothing else precedes or follows the records
· Every C line has exactly 9 bars / 10 columns
· Day is a digit 1-7; hours are two digits (08:00, not 8:00)
· The weeks column only ever shows S-E, S-E单, S-E双, S-E定 or S定
· Names match the timetable verbatim; nothing was invented

========== 5. Example output ==========

#sleepy-v1
T|2026-03-02
N1|08:00|08:45
N2|08:55|09:40
N3|10:00|10:45
N4|10:55|11:40

@format_wakeup_share_spec: Copy the whole share text, including the 【来自WakeUp课程表】 header line
The text must contain a courseDetailJson field (WakeUp adds it automatically)
Table name, semester start date and per-course colors are imported too
@format_wakeup_json_spec: The whole text must be JSON: starts with { and contains a courses array
Top level: name (table name), startDate (2026-09-07 format)
Each course: name, teacher, position (room), day (number 1-7, 1=Monday), startNode (first period), step (how many periods), startWeek/endWeek range, type (0 weekly / 1 odd / 2 even)
@format_ics_spec: Text must start with BEGIN:VCALENDAR — dropping the first line breaks recognition
Each class is one event: SUMMARY = course name, LOCATION = room; teacher is read from the description
Weekday is derived from the event date; week 1 = the Monday of the earliest event\'s week
Periods are read from the "第X - Y节" line in the description, or estimated from start/end times
@format_csv_spec: First line is the header. Required columns: course (course/name), day (day/weekday), node, week (week/weeks)
Optional columns: teacher, room, type, note
Node, two ways: one column like 1-2, or split into "start node" + "end node" columns
Week supports 1-16, 2-5,7-9, 11,13,15 — multiple ranges become separate courses
Optional "start time" + "end time" columns (HH:mm): real period times are applied automatically on import
@format_html_spec: Text must start with a tag like <!DOCTYPE, <html, or <table — any plain text before it breaks detection, delete it first
The page must contain a table whose header row includes "course"
Column names same as CSV: course, day, node, week required; teacher, room, type, note optional
Same as CSV: optional "start time" + "end time" columns, applied automatically on import
Grid layouts with Monday-Sunday columns cannot be parsed; needs a long table with one course per row
@format_plain_spec: Course line layout: Cname|day|nodes|weeks|teacher|room|color|note|time|group - exactly 10 columns / 9 pipes
Empty columns stay empty, but the pipes must not be dropped
Day is 1-7 (Monday=1); nodes as a range 1-2, or a single node 6
Week column has five shapes: 1-16 (weekly), 1-15单 (odd), 2-16双 (even), 3-4定 (range), 10定 (single week)
Leave color empty for auto; time column only for courses with a fixed clock time, as HH:mm-HH:mm
Escape | \ \" < { ( in text with a leading backslash
Period-time line (optional): N<number>|start|end, e.g. N3|10:00|10:45; or a single Nd line when times equal the built-in preset
Table line (optional): Tname|startDate|totalWeeks|nodesPerDay; startDate must be the Monday of week 1
Unrecognized lines are listed in the import preview, never silently dropped
